words.graded: Each one graded against the best games of everyone else in its era, 15 seasons either side.
words.most: Most land close to the curve: the typical level of the best in each era.
words.five: Only 6 of 4,364 are more than 5 standard deviations above it.
words.axis: score: standard deviations above the curve

caps: Picture a class test. One student scores 95. Leave them out, and take the five best scores by everyone else: about 80.
Do the same for the 15 classes before and the 15 after. The line through all those top fives is the curve.
A year with an easier test is scaled down first, just as every season is converted to the same scoring level.
The top scores usually sit within about 3 points of the curve: one standard deviation.
The 95 is 15 points above the curve: 15 ÷ 3 = 5 standard deviations. On our scale, a score of 5.
If the top fives around it had scored about 92, the same 95 would be (95 − 92) ÷ 3 = 1 standard deviation up: a score of 1.
Same score, different era. So every game in this film is graded against the best of everyone else in its own era.
